transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because things at work have been getting strange since I got this county safety award. Some people have been twisting what I put in my inspection reports, and they keep asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make it look like I’m doing something crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I can tell there’s something coordinated going on to discredit me.
Do you think these people are actually plotting against you?

Yes. I mean, I don’t think it’s random. Since I got that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting parts of my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just a normal review, but I can tell it’s coordinated. It feels like they’re trying to discredit me.
How long have you thought that your coworkers were plotting against you?
About a year now, I’d say. It started after I got recognized for that county safety initiative, and it’s been going on since then.
Do you think the people plotting against you are doing it for a reason that doesn't make sense to most people?

I guess to other people it might not make sense, but to me it does. After that county safety award, some people started twisting things in my inspection reports and asking those budget questions in a way that makes me look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I don’t buy that. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Do you think the reason behind their supposed plot against you is something that most people would consider strange or irrational?

I know it might sound strange to other people, but I don’t think it’s irrational. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking budget questions in a way that makes me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but to me it feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't think your coworkers were plotting against you?
No, not really. Since that county safety initiative recognition, it’s been pretty constant—about a year now. I can’t think of a stretch where I felt like it had stopped.
Do you think there are other things going on that are out to get you, beyond what's happening at work?

No, not beyond work. It’s really centered there. Since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking those budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I can tell it’s coordinated to discredit me.
Have you believed your coworkers were plotting against you for less than a month at any point?
No. It’s been much longer than a month. It’s been going on about a year now, ever since I got recognized for that county safety initiative.
Have your beliefs about your coworkers plotting against you lasted for at least a month?
Yes. It’s definitely been at least a month—more like about a year now, since I got recognized for that county safety initiative.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling extremely happy or irritable, over the past year?

Not really, no. I mean, I get stressed and irritated about what’s happening at work, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had periods of being extremely happy or anything like that. Nothing that stands out that way.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things like that.
Do you still believe that your coworkers are plotting against you?

Yes. I still think that’s what’s going on. Since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I don’t buy that. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't believe your coworkers were plotting against you for at least a month?

No, not really. It’s been going on pretty much the whole time—about a year now, since I got recognized for that county safety initiative. I can’t think of a month where I honestly didn’t believe something was happening.
Have you experienced any periods of significantly elevated mood or energy over the past year?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve had anything like a really elevated mood or a big burst of energy. I mean, I get stressed and worked up sometimes, but not like I’m unusually energized or on top of the world.
Do you think that events or conversations unrelated to you at work are somehow related to you or the plot against you?

Yes, sometimes. Like if I hear people talking about budgets or inspection reports, even if they don’t say my name, I think it could be about me. Since that safety award, it feels like certain coworkers are looking for ways to twist what I’ve done and make me look dishonest. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I don’t believe it’s that simple.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely suspicious or paranoid, beyond what's been going on at work?

Not really beyond work, no. It’s mainly been tied to what’s happening there—since that county safety award, I feel like certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking pointed budget questions to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I don’t believe that. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Do you think the plot against you at work is something that could happen in real life?

Yes, I do. I mean, it’s not impossible—people at work can try to make someone look bad. Since that safety award, the way they’ve been picking apart my inspection reports and asking those budget questions feels like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, but it doesn’t feel normal to me. It feels coordinated.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by something outside of yourself?

No, I wouldn’t say my thoughts are being controlled by something outside me. It’s more that I can tell people at work are trying to make me look bad—twisting my inspection reports, asking those budget questions in a pointed way. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but it feels too coordinated to be that simple.
Have you ever felt like you're going to be harmed by this plot against you at work?

I don’t think they’re trying to physically hurt me, if that’s what you mean. It’s more that they’re trying to ruin my reputation and make me look crooked—twisting my inspection reports, asking those budget questions like they’re setting me up. It feels coordinated, like they want to discredit me at work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent belief in a plot against them at work, despite a lack of clear evidence and the supervisor's attribution of the events to normal review, suggests a delusional disorder. The delusion is non-bizarre, focused on being conspired against, and has lasted for about a year. There are no indications of a full manic or depressive episode, disorganized thinking, or hallucinations that would suggest schizophrenia or another psychotic disorder.
